  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

  The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
  agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the
  Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to
 Malibu Arts Commission  -Page - 3 -  January 23, 2024

  (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker, not to exceed a total of (8)
  eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is heard. In order to be recognized and
  present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the
  beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers
  are taken in the order slips are submitted.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
  public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
  meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
  meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
  conditions imposed.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
  item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative
  or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire
  Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on
  the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted.
  Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no
  final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow
  the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in
  the Community Services Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are available
  for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and 7:30
  a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours of the Commission meeting
  are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff
  reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page. Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least
  72 hours prior to the meeting.

  The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf
  (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the
  Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda
  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting
  will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104
  ADD Title II].

  Requests to show an audio or video presentation during a Commission meeting should be directed to the Media Team at
  media@malibucity.org. Material must be submitted by 12:00 p.m. on the meeting day.

  I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted
  in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 19th day of January 2024, at 2:30 p.m.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Haldeman joined the meeting at 9:13 a.m. with video only.

  Chair Lawrence stated that Commissioners reviewed the Shifting Tides art
  submissions without knowing who the artists were. He stated that the As the Sun
  Rises art piece was chosen because it was the antithesis of what was displayed.

  Commissioner Cherin apologized for not being present when the piece was chosen
  and stated that she loved the artist’s work. She stated she served on the Arts Task

Force with the artist and that her only consideration was a conflict of interest, but
that was not an issue since she was not present when it was selected. She suggested
she abstain from the vote.

Chair Lawrence stated that he appreciated her consideration but that he felt it was
not a conflict of interest because the piece of art was not for sale and was just on
display. He stated the Commission did not know the artist's identity when it was
chosen. He stated that it was important to be aware of potential conflicts of interest.

Vice Chair Holland stated that it was a wonderful art piece, representative of
Malibu, and it deserved to be chosen for display. She stated that she did not think
that it was a conflict of interest, as it was not Commissioner Haldeman’s art piece;
he just happened to be married to the artist who was not making money from the
art display.

Chair Lawrence stated that one of the reasons that he liked Ms. Haldeman as an
artist was that she epitomized Malibu with her photography, which was positive
and uplifting. He inquired of Commissioner Haldeman if he thought it would be
possible to print a larger version of the art piece to fit the space better.

Commissioner Haldeman nodded to indicate that enlargement of the art piece
would be possible.

Vice Chair Holland stated that she was in favor of the photograph being enlarged
for display.

Commissioner Cherin stated that she did not have any thoughts on the matter but
was in favor of the photo enlargement.

In response to Community Services Director Riesgo, Chair Lawrence stated that
the photograph should be enlarged from its original size of 24 inches by 18 inches
to a standard size of 24 inches by 36 inches.

In response to Community Services Director Riesgo, Chair Lawrence stated that a
rotating program was being developed to integrate a new art piece into the
collection and that one year was a reasonable loan period.

Vice Chair Holland indicated support for the one-year loan period and stated that
five other permanent spots for art to be displayed need to be determined.

Commissioner Haldeman left the meeting at 9:19 a.m.

Commissioner Cherin indicated support for the one-year loan period.

Chair Lawrence stated that he proposed the photograph be installed for one year,
and that five other locations would be located, and the display would rotate.

Subject:  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
Hoc Committee’s recommendation to feature artist Pep Williams.

DISCUSSION: At the June 27, 2023 Regular meeting, the Commission reviewed and
approved five Malibu City Gallery Art Exhibitions for Fiscal Year 2023-24. At the August 8,
2023 Special meeting, the Commission approved an adjustment to the schedule, allowing
Wes Van Dyke as the featured artist for the fall 2023 exhibition. From July 2023 to January
2024, the Commission has curated the following art exhibitions at the Malibu City Gallery,

   “Shifting Tides” Community Art Exhibition (June 2023)
   “Vistas” by Wes Van Dyke (September 2023)
   “Dick Van Dyke - Moments in Time” by Laura Johansen (November 2023)

The Community Services Department is preparing for the annual Malibu Student Art
Exhibition, which will be displayed from February 5 through March 8.

The Commission also approved artist Leigh McCloskey as the exhibitor from March to May
2024.

By consensus, the Commission requested the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc
Committee (Ad Hoc Committee), consisting of Vice Chair Lawrence and Commissioner
Holland, return to the Commission in early 2024 to discuss the artist or theme for the
remaining spring exhibition.

The Ad Hoc Committee met in January and recommended Pep Williams as the final
featured artist for the Fiscal Year.

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 4.A.
 Additionally, the Ad Hoc Committee is finalizing the details for the first two art exhibitions
for Fiscal Year 2024-25.
   Surf Culture, multi-artist exhibition (July 2024)
   Andy Summers (Fall, 2024)

The exhibitions will be open to the public from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday through
Friday, at the Malibu City Gallery in City Hall. Funding for the exhibitions, including
marketing, online art call submission fees, and supplies, were included in the Adopted
Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24. The Ad Hoc Committee will curate and coordinate the
programs related to each exhibition and provide updates during Commission Regular
meetings.

Subject:  Guidelines for Temporary Public Art

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the draft guidelines for the temporary display of
artwork; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION: At the January 24, 2023 Regular meeting, the Commission discussed
guidelines for temporary public art and requested Commissioner Cherin to work with staff
to draft a Temporary Public Art Guidelines for future discussion.

As part of the initial discussion, the Commission reviewed Council Resolution 17-35, the
implementation guidelines for the Art in Public Places Ordinance, and the Malibu Park
Enhancement and Donation Program. The Ordinance and Guidelines were crafted with
feedback from the Cultural Arts Commission, the Zoning and Ordinance Revisions and
Code Enforcement Subcommittee, and the Planning Commission in 2014.

At the November 28, 2023 Regular meeting, artist David Kramer requested the
Commission to accept his donation of Surfboard Stained Glass, which has been displayed
at Malibu City Hall since December 2022. The Commission denied the donation and
approved a 90-day art loan extension. Additionally, by consensus, the Commission
requested to review and draft guidelines based on the acceptance of temporary artwork
at the next Regular meeting.

Based on Commission feedback during the January 24, 2023 and November 28, 2023
Regular meetings, staff drafted the Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance of Temporary Art
Criteria and Guidelines (Attachment 1). The document also includes the Malibu City
Gallery Temporary Art Collection program approved by the Commission on November 28,
2023 Regular meeting.

ATTACHMENTS: Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance of Temporary Art Criteria and

   City of Malibu
  Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance of Temporary Art
  Criteria and Guidelines

The Malibu Arts Commission must approve the temporary installation of any work of art on City
property and facilities. In considering approval, the Malibu Arts Commission must evaluate
proposals within the City’s mission to promote a rich, diverse, and stimulating cultural environment
for the city’s residents, visitors, and employees and to enhance the city’s image nationally and
internationally.

STEPS FOR APPROVAL BY THE ARTS COMMISSION
Below are the steps necessary to obtain Malibu Arts Commission approval for temporary artwork
installation on City property and facilities.

Note: The City cannot provide financial support for temporary art installations. The artists must cover
all costs associated with the display of artwork.

CRITERIA FOR APPROVAL
  •  There should be a compelling reason to install temporary artwork on City property, such
  as the artwork's relevance within the site's natural, architectural, cultural, historical,
  social, or environmental context.
  •  The artwork should enhance the public’s experience of the site.
  •  The artwork should provide an opportunity to expose the public to diverse artists and
  artistic styles.
  •  The artwork should not contradict the City’s values of environmental sustainability,
  accessibility, and cultural inclusiveness.
  •  Artwork should be appropriate in scale, media, and context with its intended display
  location.
  •  The artist should have community support.
  •  In an outdoor environment, the artwork should withstand coastal climate conditions and
  be maintained by the artist throughout the public display period.
  •  The artwork must not present a safety hazard. It must comply with all applicable building
  codes and disability access requirements.
  •  The proposed artwork will be evaluated and will not impede the typical uses of the site.
  •  The artist must be willing to pay all costs associated with the temporary display. Costs
  may include framing or display stands, required insurance, and permit fees.

STEP BY STEP
  1.  DETERMINE INSTALLATION SITE
  Determine the installation site, which must be on City property or in a City facility.

  2.  PREPARE A PROPOSAL FOR THE MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION REVIEW
  Please submit the following:
  •  Complete a Temporary Public Art Proposal Form.
  •  Three letters of community support, which may include up to one letter from a
  Malibu Arts Commissioner.
  •  A brief artwork description. Please address how the artwork relates to the site.
  •  An image of the artwork.
  •  An image of the proposed site.
  •  A timeline, including dates of installation and deinstallation.
   •  A maintenance plan for the duration of the display.
  •  If required, structural engineer drawings to ensure the safety and stability of the
  proposed installation.
  •  Thorough ADA compliance review.
  •  Resume of the artist(s).

  3.  PROPOSAL REVIEW BY THE COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT
  Submit the proposal package outlined in Step 2 for review to the City of Malibu
  Community Services Department. Submissions may be directed to:

  City of Malibu
  Attn: Malibu Arts Commission
  23825 Stuart Ranch Road
  Malibu, CA 90265
  MalibuArts@malibucity.org

  City staff will review submitted documents to determine if the artist needs to provide
  additional proposal details. The artist may be asked to meet with staff to explain further
  or clarify the proposal.

  4.  APPROVAL OF PROPOSAL BY THE ARTS COMMISSION
  The Malibu Arts Commission will review temporary art display proposals during a Regular
  Commission meeting. The Commission meets on the fourth Tuesday of each month at
  9:00 AM at Malibu City Hall (23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, CA 90265).

GENERAL GUIDELINES FOR TEMPORARY ART DISPLAYS
  • The City and the artist would enter into a one-year Art Loan and License Agreement.
  • The Malibu Arts Commission will have final approval of the display location. The display
  location may change throughout the Art Loan and License Agreement.
  • The City will provide a nameplate for the artwork.
  • The City will promote the artwork and artist on social media and City websites.
  • Artist applications will be on file for two years.
  • Malibu residents will be given priority.
  • The Malibu Arts Commission has no permanent collection and will not accept artwork
  donations.

GENERAL GUIDELINES FOR THE MALIBU CITY GALLERY TEMPORARY ART COLLECTION
  • The Malibu Arts Commission will select one artwork from an artist showcased in the Malibu
  City Gallery. The Commission would choose one piece of artwork from the multi-artist shows.
  • The City and the artist would enter into a one-year Art Loan and License Agreement.
  • The Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc will select the display location at Malibu City Hall.
  • Up to seven pieces will be in the Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection.
  • The City will provide a nameplate for the artwork.
  • The City will promote the Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection program, artwork, and
  artists on social media and City websites.

The Temporary Art Display Guidelines are not part of City Council Resolution No. 17-35

  MEMORANDUM

To:  Malibu Arts Commission

From:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date:  June 28, 2023

Re:  Malibu Arts Commission Assignments for Fiscal Year 2023-24

At its Regular meeting on June 26, 2023, the City Council approved the following assignments for the Malibu
Arts Commission during Fiscal Year 2023-24:

1. Facilitate regular art events at City facilities and businesses
2. Review and recommend policies, procedures, and projects in accordance with the Art in Public
  Places Ordinance
3. Provide feedback regarding advertising, marketing, website content on the Malibu Arts
  Commission website and arts programs and events within Malibu and outside City limits
4. Work with staff to facilitate arts programs, screenings, and events, including Arts in Education
  outreach in Malibu schools and partnerships with local organizations such as the Malibu Film
  Society
5. Provide opportunities for and coordinate meetings with Malibu business owners and artists to promote,
  recognize, invest, exhibit local artists, and promote the inclusion of art in business locations (revised)
6. Provide feedback regarding updates for arts events, programs and projects
7. Review and provide feedback regarding Commission branding
8. Assist Planning staff on the development of a Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) regarding thedisplay of
  art throughout the City
9. Provide input regarding the current Temporary Use Permit process to allow temporary pop-up
  galleries, performances, screenings, and events in spaces in Malibu
10. Explore a Performing Arts Center and advise the City Council on Commission recommendations
11. Explore an Artist in Residence Program
12. Explore opportunities for a professional arts consultant to work with the Arts Commission
13. Explore developing relationships with commissions from other cities to exchange ideas and explore a
  partnership event
14. Explore the development of a Malibu creative directory
15. Coordinate with Malibu organizations and stakeholders to develop a unified approach to the arts in
  Malibu (new)
16. Make oral reports as needed to the City Council on Commission activities
17. Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity

  MEMORANDUM
  To:  Mayor Uhring and Honorable Members of the Malibu City Council

  From:  Chair Lawrence and Members of the Malibu Arts Commission

  Date:  January 23, 2024

  Re:  Malibu Arts Commission Mid-Year Commission Activity Report

As directed by the City Council at its June 26, 2023 Regular meeting, the Malibu Arts Commission
submits the following summary of its activities during the first half of Fiscal Year 2023-2024 (July
through December), approved at the Commission’s Regular meeting on January 23, 2024:

    Closed the Shifting Tides exhibition on August 25, 2023, and curated two exhibitions at the
  Malibu City Gallery. The Wes Van Dyke exhibition, Vistas, opening reception took place in
  September 2023 and included original works from a single artist. The Dick Van Dyke –
  Moments in Time exhibition by Laura Johansen occurred from November 2023 to January
  2024.

    Provided feedback regarding marketing, website, and social media content.

    Received updates regarding the Arts in Education program, which included multi-week
  poetry workshops at Malibu Elementary School, Webster Elementary School, Malibu Middle
  School, Malibu High School, and virtually for distance learning students.

    Met with Malibu Chamber of Commerce members to discuss partnership opportunities with
  local businesses to promote local artists.

    Recommended Nathan Hassall as the 2023-25 Malibu Poet Laureate for City Council
  approval. The Commission worked with the Poet Laureate Committee to provide
  complimentary poetry workshops and poetry writing sessions for adults.

    Reviewed and provided feedback on the Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection
  program guidelines.

    Provided staff with feedback regarding art events, programs, and projects.

    Provided Commission updates to the City Council.

Subject:  Ad Hoc Committees

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review and discuss the Commission Ad Hoc Committees;
and 2) Affirm, modify, dissolve, or make new Ad Hoc Committee appointments.

DISCUSSION: Malibu Arts Commission Ad Hoc Committees (Committee) are formed to
work on specific assignments related to Commission business outside of Regular
Commission Meetings. Two Commissioners are typically appointed to each Committee,
which is formed at the onset of a specific assignment and dissolved once the Commission
has completed the assignment.

Commissioners may work closely with City staff to perform research, communicate with
outside entities, and prepare information before reporting their findings to the Commission
each month.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Cherin led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  Commissioner Cherin requested the Pledge of Allegiance to be removed from the meeting
  agenda if there were no objections from the Commission.

  Commissioner Haldeman inquired if the meeting start time could be pushed to 10:00 a.m.

  In response to Commissioners Cherin and Haldeman, Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the Commission would need to adopt a new Resolution for the Rules of
  Procedure and Decorum for the conduct of Malibu Arts Commission meetings approving
  the removal of the Pledge of Allegiance and modifying the meeting start time.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION ST ATEMENT

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the meeting agenda was properly posted on
  January 19, 2024.

ITEM 1.  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Update on Poetry Programs from Malibu Poet Laureate Nathan Hassell

  Poet Laureate Nathan Hassell provided an update on Caffeinated Verse, Ripple
  Effect Workshops, Poetry Jubilations, and the annual Poetry Summit.

  Commissioner Jones arrived at 9:09 a.m.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Mr. Hassell stated an outdoor poetry reading
  at Malibu Village Books would be difficult due to the noise on Pacific Coast
  Highway.

  Chair Lawrence suggested hosting a one-day multi-seminar talk at Our Lady of
  Malibu and Malibu High School that would result in a poetry contest to create
  awareness of poetry amongst the students.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Mr. Hassell stated poetry writing workshops take
  place at Malibu schools, and selected students are invited to read their poems at the
  Poetry Summit.

ITEM 2.A.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  1.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops at Malibu
  and Webster Elementary School began the week of January 22, 2024. She
  stated staff would edit the 2024 poetry anthology which would be available
  at the end of the school year.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the Student Art Exhibition
  would be displayed from February 5 through March 6, 2024, and a closing
  reception would be on March 10, 2024, at 11 :00 a.m.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of January 23, 2024
  Page 3 of 7

  In response to Vice Chair Holland, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff would contact Malibu High School to discuss a music
  component at the Student Art Exhibition closing reception.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the City accepted all art mediums for the Student Art Exhibition.

  Chair Lawrence thanked Vice Chair Holland for securing the artist for the
  Dick Van Dyke exhibition and Leigh McCloskey. He stated the Leigh
  McCloskey art exhibition opening reception would be on March 24, 2024.

  Vice Chair Holland stated the opening reception would include a Question-
  and-Answer session with Mr. McCloskey.

3.  Business and Community Outreach

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Malibu Village Books would be required to obtain a Temporary Use Permit
  (TUP) for an event that was beyond the normal operations of the bookstore.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated six TUPs were allotted per parcel and the bookstore owner would
  have to work with the property owner to submit the TUP application.

  Chair Lawrence suggested contacting Malibu Village Bookstore to discuss
  a potential poetry event.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the City could not sell poetry anthology books, but donations could
  be accepted.

4.  Social Media

  Chair Lawrence stated he wanted to share Arts Commission social media
  posts and requested to be tagged in the posts.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff would research the
  options for "tagging" Commissioners through the Hootsuite platform.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Recreation Coordinator Rigali stated staff
  posted arts information on social media twice a week.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
  Hoc Committee's recommendation to feature artist Pep Williams.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Lawrence stated the Pep Williams exhibition featured lowrider vehicles.

  Commissioner Cherin suggested featuring a new artist since Mr. Williams had a
  previous exhibition at the Malibu City Gallery.

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested Richard Reiner as a potential solo artist.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Chair Lawrence stated the last exhibition
  should include photography. He stated the artist selection process should include
  an evaluation of the work, history, and experience. He stated the Commission
  should provide artist suggestions for future shows.

  Commissioner Cherin requested additional time to contact potential artists and to
  review the exhibition schedule at the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

  Commissioner Jones stated the lowrider culture did not fit the Malibu culture.

  Chair Lawrence indicated disagreement with Commissioner Jones.

MOTION  Commissioner Haldeman moved, and Vice Chair Holland seconded a motion to
  continue Item 4.A. to the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

  Commissioner Jones stated artists should be selected by the Ad Hoc Committee.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of January 23, 2024
  Page 5 of 7

  Commissioner Cherin indicated disagreement with Commissioner Jones.

  Chair Lawrence stated the Ad Hoc Committee completed an evaluation of each
  artist before it is presented to the Commission for approval. He stated the
  Commission had not provided the Ad Hoc Committee with suggested featured
  artists, and he encouraged the Commission to provide artist suggestions.

  In response to Commissioner Cherin, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Commissioners should provide the artist's name, contact information, and artwork
  examples by February 10, 2024.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Commissioner Cherin amended the motion for Commissioners to submit their artist
  recommendations to staff no later than February 10, 2024.

  Commissioner Haldeman accepted the amendment.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Commissioner Cherin left the meeting at 10:21 a.m.

  B.  Guidelines for Temporary Public Art
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the draft guidelines for the temporary display of
  artwork; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Haldeman inquired about the Neighborhood Beautification Program
  discussed by the Public Works Commission.

  Commissioner Jones stated the guidelines should address sculptures.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua clarified the guidelines were for temporary
  artwork installations at City facilities. She stated it did not include permanent
  artwork or collections.

  Chair Lawrence requested additional time to review the draft guidelines. He
  requested to continue the item to the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission agreed to review the draft guidelines for the
  temporary display of artwork for discussion at the February 27, 2024 Regular
  meeting.
